Read a "French" CSV file

Source: R/import.R
read_cohort_csv.Rd

Robust reader for CSV files exported by French versions of spreadsheet software: ; separator, possible , decimal mark, several missing-value codes, automatic encoding detection (UTF-8 or Latin-1 / Windows-1252). Character columns that are actually numeric (e.g. "12,5") are converted.

Usage

read_cohort_csv(
  path,
  sep = ";",
  na = c("", "NA", "NaN", ".", "NR", "ND"),
  convert_comma_decimal = TRUE,
  encoding = "auto",
  ...
)

Arguments

path

Path to the file (accents resolved with path_resolve_nfc()).

sep

Field separator.

na

Strings read as missing values.

convert_comma_decimal

Convert character columns whose every non-missing value is a number written with a comma or a point.

encoding

"auto" (UTF-8 if the file is valid UTF-8, "latin1" otherwise) or an explicit file encoding.

...

Passed to utils::read.csv().

Value

A data frame (column names unchanged, see clean_colnames()).

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "cohort_messy.csv", package = "vernissage")
raw <- read_cohort_csv(f)
#> Detected encoding: "latin1".
str(raw)
#> 'data.frame':	6 obs. of  8 variables:
#>  $ Numéro patient: chr  "P001" "P002" "P003" "P004" ...
#>  $ Groupe        : chr  "Placebo" "Actif" "Placebo" "Actif" ...
#>  $ Sexe          : chr  "F" "M" "M" "F" ...
#>  $ Âge           : int  64 71 58 66 73 61
#>  $ NfL V0        : num  12.4 18.9 9.7 NA 21.3 11
#>  $ NfL V3        : num  13.1 NA 10.2 14.8 22.6 11.5
#>  $ Score MoCA V0 : int  27 24 29 26 NA 28
#>  $ Commentaire   : chr  "RAS" "prélèvement hémolysé" NA NA ...
